privacyPolicy.title: Privacy Policy
privacyPolicy.intro: This policy explains what data this website processes, why, and for how long.

sections.title: 1. Controller
sections.text: This website is operated by Fran Aragón, Prague, Czech Republic. Contact: info@franaragondev.com.

sections.title: 2. Contact Form
sections.text: If you use the contact form, your name, email address and message are sent by email (via the Brevo email service) so that I can reply. They are not stored on this website.

sections.title: 3. Analytics (Only With Consent)
sections.text: If you accept analytics, the site uses Google Analytics 4, Vercel Web Analytics and Speed Insights, and its own visit statistics. The visit statistics record the pages and sections you view, active time on the page, actions such as sending the contact form, opening the CV or following an external link, the referring website's domain (never the full address), campaign tags in the link, your device type, browser and operating system, and an approximate location (country and region) derived by the hosting provider from your IP address. The site's own analytics application does not store your raw IP address: it is only used briefly, in hashed form, to prevent abuse. Hosting and infrastructure providers such as Vercel may process or log IP addresses as part of operating the service. The site's own visit statistics use no fingerprinting and no identifiers that persist between visits. Google Analytics may use cookies or other identifiers to recognise a browser across visits, as described in Google's documentation and in the Cookie Policy.

sections.title: 4. Purpose and Legal Basis
sections.text: Analytics are used to understand which content interests visitors and where traffic comes from. The legal basis is your consent (Art. 6(1)(a) GDPR), which you can withdraw at any time as described in the Cookie Policy. The contact form is processed to answer your request (Art. 6(1)(b) and (f) GDPR).

sections.title: 5. Retention
sections.text: Details of a single visit are kept for up to 6 hours after the visit's last activity; after that, only aggregated weekly counts remain, for up to 120 days. Short visit summaries (approximate location, device, pages viewed, traffic source) are sent to the site owner's private Telegram chat and kept there until deleted. Google Analytics data is kept according to the retention setting of the Google Analytics property.

sections.title: 6. Service Providers
sections.text: Vercel (hosting and approximate geolocation), Upstash (analytics database), Telegram (delivery of visit summaries to the site owner), Google (Google Analytics) and Brevo (email delivery). Some of them may process data outside the European Economic Area under appropriate safeguards.

sections.title: 7. Your Rights
sections.text: You have the right to access, rectify, erase or restrict processing of your data, to object, and to withdraw consent, as well as to lodge a complaint with a supervisory authority (in the Czech Republic, the ÚOOÚ). Because the visit statistics are not linked to your identity, it may not be possible to identify the records that relate to you.

about.title: Engineering products that scale.
about.description:
I'm Fran Aragón, a Software Engineer specialized in building high-performance digital products.

I design and build scalable SaaS platforms, web applications, and native mobile systems that solve real business problems. My work focuses on clean architecture, performance, and long-term maintainability.

Currently, I work as a Software Engineer designing enterprise-grade architectures and scalable systems. Previously, I stabilized core infrastructure and led frontend architecture at Solutia, and built tools at adidas’ Innovation team used in global workflows.

I am also the founder behind HomeStocker, a native iOS ecosystem for smart inventory management.

Based in Prague. Working with companies worldwide.

overview.title: Overview
overview.paragraph: Baguira Suites Experiences is a luxury hospitality platform designed to elevate the digital presence of a boutique hotel in Calais, France. The project combines immersive storytelling, technical SEO, multilingual architecture and reservation workflows within a high-performance Next.js ecosystem.

challenge.title: The Challenge
challenge.paragraph1: Baguira required more than a website. The goal was to build a digital experience capable of reflecting the premium positioning of the brand while establishing a scalable technical foundation for future growth.
challenge.paragraph2: The platform needed to combine performance, technical SEO, online reservations, Airbnb and Booking.com multi-channel synchronization, internationalization and immersive visual storytelling without compromising Core Web Vitals.

architecture.title: Architecture
architecture.paragraph: The platform was built using Next.js App Router, TypeScript and a fully internationalized content architecture. Beyond the public-facing experience, the system integrates external hospitality infrastructure to synchronize reservations across multiple channels while providing a private environment for operations, reporting and day-to-day management. Every technical decision was focused on long-term maintainability, scalability and performance.

results.title: Results
results.paragraph: The platform achieved Lighthouse scores of 96 on mobile and 98 on desktop while maintaining an immersive visual experience and a technical SEO foundation designed to maximize international visibility.

philosophy.title: Engineering Philosophy
philosophy.quote: Engineering luxury experiences requires the same discipline as engineering enterprise systems: architecture first, aesthetics second.

cdestepona.title: CD Estepona Fans
cdestepona.label: Independent Football Supporters' Platform
cdestepona.subtitle: A multi-platform product for the CD Estepona supporters' community: a public website, a native iOS app and an internal matchday system that brings live match events to fans as they happen.

meta.title: CD Estepona Fans | Multi-Platform Sports Product Case Study
meta.description: Case study of an independent football supporters' platform: trilingual web platform, native iOS app, live Matchday Control Center, push notifications and Live Activities.

overview.title: Overview
overview.paragraph: CD Estepona Fans is an independent product for supporters of CD Estepona, a Spanish football club competing in Segunda RFEF. What began in 2025 as a news website has grown into a digital ecosystem: a trilingual web platform, a native iOS app published on the App Store, a native Android app in closed testing, and an internal Matchday Control Center where operators record every match event live.
overview.role: I own the product end to end: product direction, UX, architecture, backend, web, iOS and Android development, releases and day-to-day operation. It is an independent supporters' initiative rather than a commission from the club, which made it a genuine exercise in product ownership: every decision, from the data model to the App Store release, was mine to make and to maintain.

challenge.title: The Challenge
challenge.paragraph1: Supporters of lower-league clubs rarely get the digital experience that fans of top-flight teams take for granted. The goal was to give them one place for news, fixtures, standings, squad information and, above all, live match coverage, while keeping the operating cost proportionate to an independent project.
challenge.paragraph2: That meant solving real product problems: match data that has to be right the first time because it triggers push notifications, corrections that must never alert fans twice, a live experience that runs on serverless infrastructure, and several platforms that have to tell exactly the same story in three languages.

ecosystem.title: The Ecosystem
ecosystem.paragraph: Each surface has a clear job, and all of them share one backend and one versioned API contract.

items.name: Website
items.description: Trilingual Next.js platform for news, fixtures, standings, squads, galleries and fan games.

items.name: iOS App
items.description: Native SwiftUI app with a live Match Centre, topic-based push alerts, Home Screen widgets and Live Activities.

items.name: Android App
items.description: Native Kotlin and Jetpack Compose app built to feature parity with iOS. Not yet publicly available.

items.name: Matchday Control Center
items.description: Operator console where a dedicated matchday operator records goals, cards, substitutions and lineups during each game.

items.name: Content Admin
items.description: Editorial CMS for news, galleries, squads and fixtures, with automated translation of articles.

architecture.title: Architecture
architecture.paragraph: A single Next.js and TypeScript backend serves the website, the content admin, the Matchday Control Center and a versioned mobile API consumed by both native apps. PostgreSQL with Prisma holds the domain model, push notifications are delivered through APNs and Firebase Cloud Messaging, and iOS Live Activities are updated remotely from the server. The architecture deliberately favours a small number of well-understood moving parts that one engineer can operate reliably.

items.title: Live data from a Matchday Control Center
items.text: Live match data does not come from a third-party feed. A dedicated operator assigned to each match records every goal, card, substitution and lineup in an internal console. Minutes are derived from a server-side match clock instead of being typed, each operator can only act on the matches assigned to them, and every action is written to an audit log.

items.title: One pipeline for every data source
items.text: Operator actions are replayed through the same ingestion pipeline built for external data providers. Recording, correcting or cancelling an event becomes an insert, an update or a retraction on a single canonical timeline, and the score is always recomputed from that timeline rather than edited by hand.

items.title: Notifications that fire exactly once
items.text: Alerts are queued with a unique deduplication key and dispatched after the operator's request completes, so a slow push service never blocks the console. Historical corrections are applied idempotently and silently, without notifying fans a second time.

items.title: Real time without real-time infrastructure
items.text: Instead of maintaining socket servers, the apps poll a live endpoint whose cadence the server sets by match state: every 10 seconds during play and far less often otherwise. Every request is a conditional ETag request, so unchanged data costs a header exchange instead of a payload.

items.title: Present on the Lock Screen
items.text: On iOS, Live Activities and Home Screen widgets keep the score visible without opening the app, with the Live Activity updated remotely from the server as events are recorded.

items.title: Native on both platforms, one contract
items.text: SwiftUI on iOS and Kotlin with Jetpack Compose on Android, built against the same versioned API, notification topics and translation catalogue, with automated test suites on the web platform and in both apps.

experience.title: The Experience
experience.paragraph: The website and the app present the same matches, news and squad in the form each context needs: rich browsing and search visibility on the web, instant alerts and glanceable live scores on the phone.
experience.note: iOS images are the app's published App Store screenshots (Spanish listing). The website image was captured from production in October 2026.

results.title: Results
results.paragraph: The website is live in three languages and the iOS app was published on the App Store in October 2026. The Android app is in closed testing on Google Play and will be added here once it is publicly available.
results.note: Lighthouse 12.8 lab scores for the production home page: median of three runs per device profile, measured on 19 October 2026. Accessibility is shown for the mobile profile.

evolution.title: What's Next
evolution.paragraph: The product keeps evolving. The next milestones are the public Android release and tighter links between the website and the apps, so that a match or an article opens directly in the app when it is installed.

philosophy.title: Product Philosophy
philosophy.quote: A sports product earns trust on matchday: the score has to be right, the alert has to arrive once, and the experience has to work on every platform fans use.
